set -u
S=${1:?scratch dir} ; shift
FH=${FORTRESS_HOME:?}
rm -rf "$S" ; mkdir -p "$S/tests" "$S/caches" "$S/tmp"
printf '\0\0\0\0' > "$S/caches/global.map"
for f in "$@" ; do cp "$f" "$S/tests/" ; done
CP=$("$FH/bin/fortress_classpath" 2>/dev/null | tail -1)
echo "# harness-one $(date -u +%FT%TZ); tree $(git -C "$FH" rev-parse --short HEAD); nproc=$(nproc); load $(cut -d' ' -f1-3 /proc/loadavg); $(java -version 2>&1 | head -1); FORTRESS_THREADS=1"
cd "$FH/ProjectFortress" && FORTRESS_THREADS=1 FORTRESS_JUNIT_VERBOSE=1 FORTRESS_CACHES="$S/caches" \
  java -Xmx768m -Xss32m -Djava.io.tmpdir="$S/tmp" -Dfortress.caches="$S/caches" -Dtests="$S/tests" \
       -Dfile.encoding=UTF-8 -cp "$CP" com.sun.fortress.tests.unit_tests.SystemJUTest 2>&1 | grep -v '^\s*at ' | sed "s#$FH/##g"
echo "exit=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
rm -rf "$S"

import List.{...}
import Random.{...}
export Executable

inOrder(g: Generator[\ZZ32\]): String = do

    for x <- seq(g) do s := s || x || "," end

    assert(n.map[\ZZ32\](fn (x: ZZ32): ZZ32 => x + 1).asString, "Nothing", "Nothing mapped is Nothing")
    assert(j.ivmap[\ZZ32\](fn (i: ZZ32, x: ZZ32): ZZ32 => i + x + 10).asString, "Just(13)", "Just(3) mapped with its index 0 is Just(13)")
    assert(m.ivmap[\ZZ32\](fn (i: ZZ32, x: ZZ32): ZZ32 => i + x + 10).asString, "Just(13)", "a Maybe holding 3 mapped with its index 0 is Just(13)")
    assert(n.ivmap[\ZZ32\](fn (i: ZZ32, x: ZZ32): ZZ32 => i + x + 10).asString, "Nothing", "Nothing mapped with its index is Nothing")

    a = array[\ZZ32\](3).fill(7)

    assert(a[1], 7, "writing to an array's copy leaves the array unchanged")
    assert(c[1], 9, "an array's copy takes the write")

    assert(MaxReduction[\ZZ32\].lift(3).asString, "Just(3)", "an associative reduction lifts its operand into Just")
    assert(LessThan CMP LessThan, EqualTo, "LessThan CMP LessThan is EqualTo")
    assert(GreaterThan CMP GreaterThan, EqualTo, "GreaterThan CMP GreaterThan is EqualTo")
    assert(LexicographicReduction.isLeftZero(LessThan), false, "today's value: the lexicographic reduction answers its inherited isLeftZero for a total comparison")
    assert(BIG MAX[x <- 0#4] x, 3, "BIG MAX over 0#4 is 3, one element")

    nested = (0#3).nest[\ZZ32\](fn (i: ZZ32): Generator[\ZZ32\] => (10 i)#2)
    assert(inOrder(seq(nested)), "0,1,10,11,20,21,", "seq of a nested generator generates the inner elements in order")
    assert(seq((0#2).cross[\ZZ32\](0#2)).asString, "seq(seq(0,1).cross(seq(0,1)))", "seq of a pair generator is the sequential pair of the two sequential generators")

    kept = (0#6).filter(fn (x: ZZ32): Boolean => x > 1)
    assert(inOrder(kept.filter(fn (x: ZZ32): Boolean => x < 5)), "2,3,4,", "a filter generator filtered again keeps the elements both predicates keep")
    mappedIndexed = (0#3).map[\ZZ32\](fn (x: ZZ32): ZZ32 => x + 1)
    twice = mappedIndexed.map[\ZZ32\](fn (x: ZZ32): ZZ32 => 10 x)
    assert(inOrder(twice), "10,20,30,", "an indexed generator mapped twice applies both functions in order")
    assert(twice[1], 20, "an indexed generator mapped twice is still indexed")
    mapped = kept.map[\ZZ32\](fn (x: ZZ32): ZZ32 => x + 1)
    assert(inOrder(mapped.map[\ZZ32\](fn (x: ZZ32): ZZ32 => 10 x)), "30,40,50,60,", "a mapped generator mapped again composes the two functions")

    increasing = relationalPredicate[\ZZ32\](fn (x: ZZ32, y: ZZ32): Boolean => x < y)
    rising = increasing(0#3)
    assert(rising.holds, true, "0, 1, 2 is increasing")

    assert(inOrder(rising.target()), "0,1,2,", "a relational predicate's target is the generator it was applied to")
    assert(increasing(<|[\ZZ32\] 2, 1|>).holds, false, "2, 1 is not increasing")

    empty = ""
    flat = "abc"
    assert(empty.split().asString, "Nothing", "the empty string splits into no pieces")
    assert(empty.splitWithOffsets().asString, "Nothing", "the empty string splits into no pieces with offsets")
    assert(flat.split().asString, "Nothing", "a flat string answers no subdivision")
    assert(flat.splitWithOffsets().asString, "Nothing", "a flat string answers no subdivision with offsets")

    assert((3:).atMost(2).asString, "[3,4]", "the left range 3: limited to two elements is [3,4]")
    assert((:3).atMost(2).asString, "[2,3]", "the right range :3 limited to two elements is [2,3]")
    assert((3:).every(2).atMost(3).asString, "[3,5,7]", "the left range 3: every second element, three of them, is [3,5,7]")

    cube = array[\ZZ32\](2,2,2).fill(5)
    cube[(1,1,1)] := 9
    moved = cube.shift((1,1,1))
    assert(moved[(2,2,2)], 9, "a three-dimensional array shifted to origin (1,1,1) holds the element of (1,1,1) at (2,2,2)")
    assert(cube.shift((0,0,0))[(1,1,1)], 9, "a three-dimensional array shifted to its own origin is unchanged")

    assert(("a" 1), "a1", "a string juxtaposed with a number appends the number's text")
    assert((1 "a"), "1a", "a number juxtaposed with a string prepends the number's text")
    assert(("a" "b"), "ab", "two juxtaposed strings concatenate")
    assert((true "x"), "truex", "a boolean juxtaposed with a string prepends its text")

    msg = seq(0#3).map[\ZZ32\](fn (x: ZZ32): ZZ32 => x + 1)
    assert(inOrder(msg.map[\ZZ32\](fn (x: ZZ32): ZZ32 => 2 x)), "2,4,6,", "a sequential mapped generator mapped again composes the two functions in order")
    nsg = seq(0#2).nest[\ZZ32\](fn (i: ZZ32): SequentialGenerator[\ZZ32\] => seq((10 i)#2))
    assert(inOrder(nsg.map[\ZZ32\](fn (x: ZZ32): ZZ32 => x + 1)), "1,2,11,12,", "a sequential nested generator mapped applies the function to each inner element in order")
    assert(inOrder(nsg.nest[\ZZ32\](fn (x: ZZ32): Generator[\ZZ32\] => x#1)), "0,1,10,11,", "a sequential nested generator nested again generates each inner element in order")
    assert(inOrder(seq(0#3).map[\ZZ32\](fn (x: ZZ32): ZZ32 => x + 10)), "10,11,12,", "today's value: a sequential range mapped generates the mapped elements in order")

    g = linearCongruential(42)
    u = UniformDistribution[\ZZ32\](1:3)
    assert(u.min[\ZZ64\](g).asString, "Just(1)", "a uniform distribution over 1:3 has minimum 1")
    assert(u.max[\ZZ64\](g).asString, "Just(3)", "a uniform distribution over 1:3 has maximum 3")
    assert(u.generate[\ZZ64\](g) IN (1:3), true, "a uniform distribution over 1:3 draws a value in 1:3")
    println("PASS")
end

end
EOF

#!/bin/bash
# The gate's checker-count stage: run the bytecode compiler's static checker over the
# INTERPRETER's library, with the interpreter's prelude in scope, and print the per-api
# error table, the total and the crash line that follows it.
#
# Why it exists: POSITIONS.md, 2026-09-21, "the library route" - one library, the
# interpreter's, becomes the library the compiler checks - and step 1 of
# coordinator/library-route-judgement.md, which makes the distance to that goal a
# permanent gate stage rather than a one-off script. A change in the count is reported, not red (checker-gate-review.md).
#
# Run from $FORTRESS_HOME with explorations/experiment/env.sh sourced, after ant compileAll:
#
#     explorations/coordinator/tools/checker-count/run.sh <out-file> [scratch-dir]
#
# It writes the table to <out-file> and prints it. Nothing in the tree is touched:
# javac output and the checker's caches go to the scratch directory (default: $TMPDIR
# or /tmp), and the caches are given to the JVM as -Dfortress.caches, honoured through
# ProjectProperties.java:261-269,283, so default_repository/ is never read or written.
# Exit 0 if the table was produced, 1 if it could not be. 20 s in the main tree,
# measured 2026-09-22; it needs no library rebuild and no warm cache.
#
# The two sources beside this script are copies, taken 2026-09-22 from
# explorations/perf-probes/prelude/, so that the gate does not depend on a probe
# directory: WorldFlip.java (Shell.useInterpreterLibraries() plus
# PhaseOrder.compilerPhaseOrder, both public, which is the world switch without an edit
# to a tracked file) and shadow-src/.../StaticChecker.java, a copy of
# ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/StaticChecker.java with three
# instrumentation points added: it names each compilation unit it checks and prints that
# unit's error count, and it catches the OverloadingChecker crash instead of dying on it.
# It is put AHEAD of ProjectFortress/build on the classpath, the technique of

content.content:
#!/bin/bash
# junit.sh <label> <dir-of-tests> <Name.test>... : the gather of climb batch N runs each .test through the
# harness in the main tree (fortress junit, the compiled test harness, as climb batch 6.5's gather ran its pair),
# in the order given, so that a link test runs before its XXX run test. Each named component's cache entries are
# removed before the list and after it. First line: the machine line (protocol.md, principle 2).
# ONE_JVM=1 (added 2026-09-29 for the repair on the merged tree, coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.md, "A repair
# of tests and records only"): the whole list in one fortress junit run, one JVM, as the gate's track runs them
# together; Shell junit hands the list to FileTests.suiteFromListOfFiles (Shell.java:1086), which puts its
# compile and link tests before its run tests (FileTests.java:997-1004), so a link test still runs first.
source "$(dirname "$0")/../../../experiment/env.sh"
FH=$FORTRESS_HOME; L=${1:?label}; D=$(cd "${2:?dir}" && pwd); shift 2
cd "$FH/ProjectFortress"
CP=$(../bin/fortress_classpath | tail -1)
echo "# junit.sh $L $(date -u +%FT%TZ); nproc $(nproc); $(grep -m1 'model name' /proc/cpuinfo | cut -d: -f2 | sed 's/^ //'); $(grep -m1 'cpu MHz' /proc/cpuinfo | cut -d: -f2 | sed 's/^ //') MHz; load at start $(cut -d' ' -f1-3 /proc/loadavg); $(java -version 2>&1 | head -1); FORTRESS_THREADS=$FORTRESS_THREADS; tree $(git -C $FH rev-parse --short HEAD)$(git -C $FH diff --quiet HEAD -- ProjectFortress Library || echo ' with the next rung applied, not yet committed'); tests from $D"
clean () { for t in "$@"; do n=$(sed -n 's/^tests=//p' "$D/$t" | head -1); [ -n "$n" ] && find ../default_repository/caches -name "*$n*" -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null; done; }
clean "$@"
if [ -n "${ONE_JVM:-}" ]; then
  files=(); for t in "$@"; do files+=("$D/$t"); done
  echo "########## [$L] fortress junit, one JVM: $*"
  java $JAVA_FLAGS -Dfile.encoding=UTF-8 -cp "$CP" com.sun.fortress.Shell junit "${files[@]}" 2>&1 | sed "s#$FH/##g" | grep -v '^\s*at ' | cut -c1-240
  echo "exit=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
else
for t in "$@"; do
  echo "########## [$L] fortress junit $t"
  java $JAVA_FLAGS -Dfile.encoding=UTF-8 -cp "$CP" com.sun.fortress.Shell junit "$D/$t" 2>&1 | sed "s#$FH/##g" | grep -v '^\s*at ' | cut -c1-240
  echo "exit=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
done
fi
clean "$@"

content.content:
\section{Subtype Rule}
\seclabel{subtype-rule}

If the parameter type of one declaration is a subtype of the parameter
type of another (and they are not the same) then there is no
ambiguity between these two declarations: for every call to which both
are applicable, the first is more specific.  This is the basis of the
Subtype Rule.

The Subtype Rule also requires a relationship between the return types
of the two declarations.  Without such a requirement, a program may
violate type safety.

\paragraph{The Subtype Rule for Functions and Functional Methods:}
Suppose that $\f(\Ps) : \Us$ and $\f(\Qs) : \Vs$ are two distinct
function or functional method declarations in a single scope.
If $\Ps \strictsubtype \Qs$ and $\Us \Ovrsubtype \Vs$ then $\f(\Ps)$ and
$\f(\Qs)$ are a valid overloading.

\paragraph{The Subtype Rule for Dotted Methods:}
Suppose that $\Ps_0.\f(\Ps) : \Us$ and $\Qs_0.\f(\Qs) : \Vs$ are two
distinct dotted method declarations provided by a trait or object $C$.
If $\Ps_0 \strictsubtype \Qs_0$, $\Ps \strictsubtype \Qs$,
and $\Us \Ovrsubtype
\Vs$ then $\Ps_0.\f(\Ps)$ and $\Qs_0.\f(\Qs)$ are a valid overloading.

\section{Incompatibility Rule}
\seclabel{incompatibility-rule}

The basic idea behind the Incompatibility Rule is that if there is no
call to which two overloaded declarations are both applicable
then there is no potential for ambiguous calls.  In such a case, we say

Partial overriding of an overloaded functional is allowed
but partial overriding of a functional declaration is not allowed.
}

A method declaration may have the modifier \KWD{override}.
Such a declaration \emph{overrides} any inherited declaration with the same name
and the self parameter (if any) at the same position,
whose parameter type, not counting the type of the self parameter,
is a strict subtype of the overriding declaration's parameter type.
The return type of the overriding declaration must be subtype of
that of the overridden declaration to preserve type safety.
A declaration with the modifier \KWD{override} must override
some inherited declaration.
It is a static error if a declaration with the modifier \KWD{override}
does not override any inherited declaration.

Here is an example trait \TYP{Enzyme} which provides methods
\VAR{reactionSpeed} and \VAR{catalyze}:
\input{\home/basic/examples/Trait.Method.e.tex}
\TYP{Enzyme}
\revision{revival-meet}{The Working Draft of February 2011 asked here, as for
functions, for a declaration on the intersection itself.}

Notice that the Meet Rule for functional methods requires the self
parameters of two overloaded declarations to be in the same position.
This requirement guarantees that no ambiguity is caused by the
position of the self parameter.  Two declarations which differ in the
position of the self parameter must satisfy either the Subtype Rule or
the Incompatibility Rule to be a valid overloading.

rangeContains(r: Range[\ZZ32\], c: Char) : Boolean

    (** Answers a subdivision of self into substrings.  This method must take time
        proportional to the number of pairs generated.   If there is no such subdivision,
        it's fine to answer the empty generator Nothing, but in this case the
        implementation of the subtrait must offer linear time indexing.
        The pairs (start, str) that are generated by this method must be such that
            start[0] = 0,      and
            start[i] = | str[0] || ... || str[i-1] |,       and
            str[0] || str [1] || ... || str[n] = self
    **)
\end{Fortress}
Because of the \KWD{comprises} clauses of $S$ and $T$ and the \KWD{excludes}
clause of $U$, any value of both $S$ and $T$ is a value of
$V$.  Thus, $V$ covers $S \inter T$, and the declaration $f(V)$
``disambiguates'' $f(S)$ and $f(T)$, i.e., it is applicable to and more
specific for any call at run time to which both $f(S)$ and $f(T)$ are
applicable.

problem: explorations/compile-ladder/gate/distance-sites.tsv:94 (copy), :109 (Maybe's ivmap), :114 (String's juxtaposition), :117 (lift), :149 to :176 (the return-type slips), :205 and :489 (the BIG operators' bodies)

precedent: Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3579-3585 (SimpleSeqFilterGenerator declares its own seq on the meet); Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2116-2135 (fill and tabulate defined where the array diamond meets); Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3527-3546 (SimpleMappedIndexed, the meet of MappedGenerator and Indexed, declares its own map); Library/FortressLibrary.fss:96 and :4346 (top-level operators whose operand is Any)
deviation: String's juxtaposition becomes three top-level operators where the team wrote three functional methods of String (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4237-4240, Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:2440-2443); every other edit is a declaration on a meet or a declared type set to what its body answers
historical: Library/FortressLibrary.fsi, Library/FortressLibrary.fss, Library/RangeInternals.fsi, Library/RangeInternals.fss, Library/String.fss, Library/FlatString.fss, Library/Random.fsi, Library/Random.fss

## 1. What changed

The branch was new; nothing was inherited. Four commits: the tests alone (`62a62f94c`, `8166315d4`), the edit (`91ed5d776`), and a follow-up the first distance run asked for (`e995c31c0`). Under Q1 = (a) the rung repaired the Meet Rule pairs one type provides, String's own juxtaposition pair and the declared-type slips, and left every top-level pair of two functional methods to rung O.

**Meet Rule pairs, declarations on the meet (P2's devices M and C, and three more):**
- `Maybe` declares `map[\G\](f: T->G): Maybe[\G\]` and `ivmap[\G\](f: (ZZ32,T)->G): Maybe[\G\]` (Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:920-921; the component's bodies at Library/FortressLibrary.fss:1441-1444, `cond` over `Just` and `Nothing` as `Condition`'s bodies do). In the api `Maybe` is the first type below both `Condition` and `ZeroIndexed` (Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:917).
- `StandardMutableArrayType` declares `copy():T` (Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1466, Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2134), abstract, where `fill` and `tabulate` already meet.
- `SimpleMappedSeqGenerator` declares `map`, answering a `SimpleMappedSeqGenerator` over the composed function (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3554-3555); `SimpleNestedSeqGenerator` declares `map`, answering a `SimpleNestedSeqGenerator` that maps each inner sequential generator, and `nest`, `NestedGenerator`'s body restated (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3635-3638). The precedent is `SimpleSeqFilterGenerator`'s own `seq` (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3584).
- `String`'s juxtaposition: the three functional methods of `String` (`(a:Any, self)`, `(self, b:String)`, `(self, b:Any)`) become three top-level operators with the same bodies (Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:2440-2443, Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4237-4240). Two functional methods with `self` at different positions satisfy neither the Subtype nor the Incompatibility Rule, and the text admits no meet for them (Specification/advanced/overloading.tex:517-523); as top-level functions the Meet Rule for functions is met by `(String, String)` (:411-415 contrasts the two rules).

**Slips, each declared type set to what its body answers (P2's S and the rest):**
- the api's `AssociativeReduction.lift(r:R)` against `ActualReduction.lift(r:R)` (Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1860); the component's `lift(r:Any)` throughout is unchanged.
- the api's `LessThan` and `GreaterThan` `CMP(self, other: LessThan|GreaterThan): TotalComparison`, as the component already declares (Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:139, :150).
- `LeftScalarRange.every: BoundedScalarRange`, `LeftScalarRange.atMost` and `RightScalarRange.atMost: FullScalarRange` (Library/RangeInternals.fsi:240, :242, :298; Library/RangeInternals.fss:563, :571, :683), and `RightScalarRange.every: BoundedScalarRange` (Library/RangeInternals.fsi:296, Library/RangeInternals.fss:675), whose body answers a `LeftScalarRange` for a negative stride.
- `FilterGenerator.filter: FilterGenerator[\E\]`, the api's own type (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3568 against Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:2101); `MappedGenerator.map: MappedGenerator[\E,G\]` (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3517). Each had declared an object type that the override in `FilterGenerator2` and `SimpleMappedIndexed` could not answer.
- `ConcreteRelationalPredicateCondition[\E\]` extends `RelationalPredicateCondition[\E\]`, not `[\()\]` (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4598); its `relation` and `target` then answer its parent's.
- `SimpleNestedGenerator.seq: SequentialGenerator[\F\]` and `SimplePairGenerator.seq: SequentialGenerator[\(E,F)\]` (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3617, :3659).
- `Array3.shift: Array[\T,(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)\]` (Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1777, Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2881); `Col` and `Row`'s `subarray: Array1[\T,b,s\]` (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2626, :2637). No code constructs a `Col` or a `Row`, so no walk program reaches the last two.
- `EmptyString` and `FlatString`'s `split(): Generator[\String\] = Nothing[\String\]` and `splitWithOffsets(): Generator[\(ZZ32,String)\] = Nothing[\(ZZ32,String)\]` (Library/String.fss:317-318, Library/FlatString.fss:146-147), the empty generator the api's comment asks for (Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:2382-2390). This is row 356.
- the unary `BIG MAX` returns `T` (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3247; row 472), and the nullary `BIG MINMAX` is a `Comprehension[\T,(T,T),(T,T),AnyMaybe\]`, as `BIG MIN_MIN`'s siblings are (Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1951, Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3259-3260; row 473).
- row 483: `UniformDistribution[\T\](range: FullRange[\T\])` (Library/Random.fsi:258, Library/Random.fss:370), so `T` is the range's element type and a `ZZ64` distribution over a `ZZ32` range is refused at construction.
- row 531: `getter avFlat(): RR32 = narrow(asFloat(ssize) / asFloat(numFlat))` (Library/String.fss:508).

**Tests.** New in `ProjectFortress/tests/`: `LibraryMeetDeclarations.fss` (every repaired declaration a program can reach, called with the value it answers, passing before and after, and two values pinned as today's), `BigMinMax.fss`, `SequentialGeneratorMap.fss`, `XXXUniformDistributionRangeType.fss`. The branch was new; nothing was inherited. Four commits: the tests alone (`62a62f94c`, `8166315d4`), the edit (`91ed5d776`), and a follow-up the first distance run asked for (`e995c31c0`). **Slips, each declared type set to what its body answers (P2's S and the rest):**
